text: When you design a REST API, keep your endpoints simple and predictable. Use nouns for resources, such as /users or /orders, and let HTTP methods show the action. Always return the correct status codes so clients understand what happened, like 200 for success or 404 when something is missing. Good documentation is essential because it helps other developers use your API quickly. You should also plan for versioning from the start, for example by adding /v1/ to your URLs, so future changes do not break existing users. These simple habits make your API easier to maintain and more pleasant to work with.
